Short answer: Rent the tool when it already fits the job. Consider a custom system when the same workaround repeats, several subscriptions duplicate one workflow, or ownership matters enough to justify building and care.

What this means for your business

Custom is not automatically cheaper, and SaaS is not automatically wasteful. Compare total cost, staff time, switching risk, data access, and who keeps the system working.

What to watch

  • Paying for several tools to move one customer through one process.
  • Copying the same information by hand.
  • A must-have workflow blocked by the product roadmap.
  • No clean export or unclear account ownership.

Do this next

  1. List every tool touching the workflow and its real annual cost.
  2. Count the repeated handoffs and corrections for one week.
  3. Ask what can be kept or connected before replacing anything.
  4. Price build, maintenance, migration, and exit together.

When Little Fight fits

We use keep, connect, replace, or build in that order. A custom system fits when the business case survives the math. Sometimes the right answer is one better spreadsheet. Glamorous? No. Useful? Very.
